title: Bobby Deol Just Delivered the Performance of His Life. Almost Nobody Was in the Theatre to See It.
excerpt: Anurag Kashyap's Bandar opened to ₹50 lakh. Then audiences started telling their friends. The TIFF-premiered prison drama is building the old-fashioned way — one stunned viewer at a time.
body:
There is a scene early in **Bandar** where **Bobby Deol**'s Samar Mehra — a fading singer-actor who once had magazine covers and fan screams — walks into a prison yard and nobody recognises him. The inmates don't care. The guards don't care. The camera holds on his face long enough for you to watch the exact moment a man realises that fame was the only thing standing between him and complete helplessness.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=4E0-K9F16r8</youtube>

It is, quietly, one of the most devastating moments in Hindi cinema this year. And it comes from the last person anyone expected.

## The Setup

Directed by **Anurag Kashyap** and written by **Sudip Sharma** and **Abhishek Banerjee**, *Bandar* follows Samar, a celebrity on the decline, whose life detonates when a woman named Gayatri (**Sapna Pabbi**) files a rape complaint against him. What follows is not a courtroom drama. It is a prison drama — grimy, claustrophobic, unrelenting — in which Samar is thrown into a system designed to break men and discovers that his name, his face, his career mean exactly nothing behind bars.

The film premiered at the **Toronto International Film Festival** in 2025. It arrives in Indian theatres now, in the middle of June's absurd nine-film pile-up, with a modest 500-600 screen release from **Zee Studios**. On Day 1, it made ₹50 lakh. On Day 2, it jumped 90% to ₹95 lakh. By Sunday, the total crossed ₹1.45 crore net.

Those numbers are tiny. The trajectory is not.

## Bobby Deol, Unmasked

For the better part of the last decade, Bobby Deol has played intimidating villains — *Animal*, *Kanguva*, the kind of roles where he shows up with a stare and a jawline and lets the background score do the rest. In *Bandar*, Kashyap strips all of that away. Deol plays vulnerability, confusion, emotional exhaustion. Samar is not particularly likeable, and the film never tries to make him so. He is arrogant and fragile in the same breath. Deol commits to every contradiction.

> "You are in the best form ever. Undoubtedly the finest actor today. Enduring and vulnerable. Way to go, bhaiya." — Esha Deol

Critics have been emphatic. **Filmfare** called it "one of the finest performances of his career." Multiple reviewers rated the film 4 to 4.5 out of 5. One X user wrote that it is "one of the most necessary films of our time" from Hindi cinema, a film that forces you to sit with discomfort rather than offering easy resolutions.

https://www.instagram.com/reel/DZMwESMIyuB/

## The Ensemble

**Sapna Pabbi** as Gayatri avoids turning the character into a simple symbol. **Sanya Malhotra** is excellent as Samar's fiercely supportive sister. **Saba Azad** brings warmth as Khushi. And then there is the prison itself — a living organism of fear and exploitation, populated by **Indrajith Sukumaran** as a calm, menacing inmate kingpin, **Jitendra Joshi** as a repulsive corrupt cop, and **Raj B. Shetty** as an eccentric prisoner who steals every scene he is in.

Kashyap shoots it with documentary-like immediacy. The prison becomes a character. The soundtrack — particularly the song *Pinjara* — rises organically from Samar's emotional wreckage without ever disrupting the narrative flow.

## The Screen-Sharing Battle

Here is the part that should make you angry. *Bandar* was never designed for a massive opening. Zee Studios asked for 3-4 shows per multiplex, after 1 PM, in chains with 4-5 screens. A modest, reasonable ask for a content-driven film. But because national chains like **PVR, Inox, and Cinepolis** are directly distributing competing films — *Hai Jawani Toh Ishq Hona Hai* and *Peddi* — *Bandar* was offered far fewer and less favourable slots. Zee Studios chose to halt programming in major chains rather than accept what they considered an unfair deal.

This is the business side of Bollywood's biggest month: nine major films, ₹1,400 crore at stake, and a film that actually has something to say getting squeezed out of the conversation by sheer volume.

## Why It Matters for the Diaspora

If you are in the US, UK, or Canada and *Bandar* is playing near you — go. This is the kind of film that rarely survives the theatrical gauntlet. It does not have a dance number. It does not have a love triangle. It has Bobby Deol sitting in a jail cell, stripped of everything that ever defined him, and discovering what is left.

In a week where Bollywood is competing for your attention with nine different films and ₹1,400 crore worth of spectacle, the most powerful thing on screen cost ₹15 crore and opened to ₹50 lakh. Word of mouth is building. The 90% Day 2 jump proves it. The question is whether enough people will find it before it disappears.

**Directed by** Anurag Kashyap. **Starring** Bobby Deol, Sanya Malhotra, Sapna Pabbi, Saba Azad, Indrajith Sukumaran. **In theatres now.**
